reason: The episode added five agents tools and a template capability, and the tool reference had to be edited by hand with no generator to keep it in step; a checklist for the class of work (new module capability) prevents the reference and template drifting next time.

The person steered the channels design toward one command with help and a one-line start message, and rejected a long prompt listing operations. That is a durable module-design preference, and this skill governs new module capabilities.

Adding the web restart verb meant editing three places beyond code and tests: the module README bullet list, the prompts.xml tools comment, and the tool reference. The checklist named only the reference.
Stop-then-start was two chances for an agent to leave the web page down; the person asked for one command, and the restart verb was built and checked on the live server.

Adding a verb that writes or reaches the network trips the effect guard test; the checklist should name the test, the command that runs it alone, and the pre-existing-failure check so the next agent does not blame its own change for dispatch_spend.
The same checklist governs removal, and the removal run had no skill telling it what to touch: a table drop, a dependency drop, snapshot and tool-reference rows, and external installs.

The episode added two nouns to an existing verb and had to find by grep that the CHANGELOG and tool reference were the places to update; the checklist only covers new verbs, so the next agent would miss the reference row.
